title: Showcase: the load test
summary: Build one bigger truss from the strongest week 7 design and load it in front of the family, with the numbers from every design on a board.
materials: hot glue gun and glue sticks, adult supervised
a small bucket or bag for the load
washers, pennies or a kitchen scale for weighing the load
tri-fold science fair board or a large sheet of card
the Maker's Log, open to week 7

steps.title: Build the showcase truss and plan the demo
steps.body:
With an adult present for the hot glue, build one larger truss using the design that held the most weight in week 7. Make it big enough to bridge a real gap, such as the space between two stacks of books or two chairs.

Plan the demo in this order.

1. Show the three week 7 designs, or their photos, and say which shape held the most weight and why.

2. Show the bigger truss and where it will bridge.

3. Load it in front of the family with a bucket or bag, adding weight until it visibly bends, without pushing it all the way to breaking on demo day.

4. Read the final weight held and compare it with the biggest week 7 number.

Write all four numbers, the three week 7 designs and the showcase truss, on the science fair board where the family can see them during the demo.

figure.alt: A larger truss bridges the gap between two stacks of books. A bucket hangs by a string from the middle of the truss, and weight is added slowly while the family watches for the point where it begins to sag.

steps.title: Rehearse the load test
steps.body:
Set the truss across its gap and add weight slowly at least once before the family sees it, watching for the point where it starts to sag. Stop well before that point so the real demo has something left to show.

Check that the board's numbers are real numbers from the Maker's Log, not rounded guesses. Also check that you can explain in one sentence why triangles carried more weight than the plain rectangle.
checklist: The bigger truss bridges its gap and was tested once before the family watches
The board shows real numbers from all three week 7 designs and the new truss
I can say in one sentence why the triangled design beat the plain rectangle
The demo has a clear stopping point before the truss is pushed to breaking

steps.title: Show the family
steps.body:
Gather the family and run the demo in the order rehearsed: the three designs and their numbers, the bigger truss, the load going on slowly, and the final weight held. Let someone else add a weight or two if they want to feel it holding.

End by naming the weakest point in the design, the spot most likely to fail first if the load kept climbing, and how you would brace it next time.

steps.title: Show it
steps.prompt: A short recording of the truss being loaded in front of the family, plus a photo of the science fair board with all four numbers
